categories.name: Media library
categories.shortDescription: Upload audio or video, fetch transcripts, get AI insights, organize, favorite, export.

tools.name: update_transcription
tools.title: Update Transcription Text
tools.description: Edit the official transcript text of a single media file by finding and replacing text. Replaces every occurrence of the original text with the replacement (leave replacement empty to delete the text) and reports how many occurrences were replaced. Use update_transcript_speakers to rename speaker labels instead.

tools.name: get_signed_upload_url
tools.title: Get Signed Upload URL
tools.description: Get a pre-signed S3 URL for direct file upload to Speak AI storage. After getting the URL, PUT your file to it, then call upload_media with the S3 URL. For a simpler workflow, use upload_local_file instead which handles all steps automatically.

tools.name: upload_media
tools.title: Upload Media from URL
tools.description: Upload media from a URL — a direct/public file URL, a pre-signed S3 URL, or a shareable social/video page link, which Speak resolves to the underlying media automatically. Supported page links: YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, X/Twitter, Facebook, Reddit, SoundCloud, Twitch, Dailymotion, Streamable, Snapchat, Pinterest, Tumblr, Bilibili, VK, OK.ru and Rutube. Vimeo and Loom page links are not supported. Processing is asynchronous — after uploading, use get_media_status to poll until state is 'processed' (typically 1-3 minutes for audio under 60 min), then use get_transcript and get_media_insights to retrieve results. For a single call that handles everything, use upload_and_analyze instead. For local files, use upload_local_file.

tools.name: upload_local_file
tools.title: Upload Local File
tools.description: Upload a local file to Speak AI for transcription and analysis. Reads the file from disk, gets a pre-signed S3 URL, uploads the file, then creates the media entry. Works with any audio or video file on the local filesystem. After upload, use get_media_status to poll for completion, then get_transcript and get_media_insights.

tools.name: upload_and_analyze
tools.title: Upload and Analyze Media
tools.description: Upload and transcribe media from a URL — a direct/public file URL, OR a shareable social/video page link, which Speak resolves to the underlying media automatically. Supported page links: YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, X/Twitter, Facebook, Reddit, SoundCloud, Twitch, Dailymotion, Streamable, Snapchat, Pinterest, Tumblr, Bilibili, VK, OK.ru and Rutube. Vimeo and Loom page links are not supported. Returns media_id immediately; after this returns, poll get_media_status until state is 'processed' (typically 1-3 min for under 60min audio), then call get_media_insights for AI summaries. This async pattern is required for remote MCP transports — long blocking calls die at proxy idle timeouts.

tools.name: list_media
tools.title: List Media Files
tools.description: List and search media files in the workspace with filtering, pagination, and sorting. Use filterName for text search, mediaType to filter by audio/video/text, folderId for folder-specific results, and from/to for date ranges. Use the include param to embed additional data (transcripts, speakers, keywords) inline with each result, avoiding N+1 API calls. Returns mediaIds you can pass to get_transcript, get_media_insights, or ask_ai_chat. For deep full-text search across transcripts, use search_media instead.

tools.name: get_media_insights
tools.title: Get Media Insights
tools.description: Retrieve AI-generated insights for a processed media file — topics, sentiment, keywords, action items, summaries, and more. The media must be in 'processed' state (check with get_media_status first). For asking custom questions about a media file, use ask_ai_chat instead.

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.title: Get Transcript
tools.description: Retrieve the full transcript for a media file with speaker labels and timestamps. Works on processed media and also returns the partial, in-progress transcript while a meeting bot is still recording (LIVE_TRANSCRIPT state). To fetch only the new sentences added since your previous call during a live meeting, use get_live_meeting_transcript instead. Use update_transcript_speakers to rename speaker labels after reviewing. For subtitle-formatted output, use get_captions instead.

tools.name: get_captions
tools.title: Get Captions
tools.description: Get captions for a media file. Captions are separate from full transcripts and are formatted for display/subtitles.

tools.name: update_transcript_speakers
tools.title: Rename Transcript Speakers
tools.description: Update or rename speaker labels in a single media transcript. Call get_transcript first to read the speaker list — a speaker's label is whatever it was last renamed to, not a fixed value, so ids from an earlier turn may be stale. Renaming a speaker to a name another speaker already has is refused as a collision. Re-sending a rename that has already been applied is a safe no-op, so do not retry a call that reported success.

tools.name: bulk_update_transcript_speakers
tools.title: Bulk Rename Speakers Across Files
tools.description: Normalise speaker names that are ALREADY correct across multiple media files — for example changing "Frederik S." to "Frederik" everywhere. Applies the same mapping to every specified media file. NOT a way to identify a speaker across a project: neither the numeric id nor a default label such as "Speaker 1" refers to the same person in different files, because speakers are numbered per file in order of appearance. Renaming "Speaker 1" across many files will label a different person in each one. Identify the speakers in each file first (get_transcript, or an identify-speakers automation), then use this tool only to tidy up naming that is already correct. Match by the speaker's current LABEL, not by numeric id. A file whose speakers do not match the mapping is left unchanged and reported as failed. Re-sending a mapping that has already been applied is a safe no-op, so do not retry a call that reported success.

tools.name: get_media_status
tools.title: Get Media Status
tools.description: Check the processing status of a media file. States: pending → transcribing → analyzing → processed (or failed). Poll this after upload_media until state is 'processed', then use get_transcript and get_media_insights to retrieve results.

tools.name: update_media_metadata
tools.title: Update Media Metadata
tools.description: Update metadata fields (name, description, tags, status) for an existing media file.

tools.name: delete_media
tools.title: Delete Media File
tools.description: Permanently delete a media file and all associated transcripts and insights.

tools.name: toggle_media_favorite
tools.title: Toggle Media Favorite
tools.description: Mark or unmark media files as favorites for quick access.

tools.name: reanalyze_media
tools.title: Re-analyze Media
tools.description: Re-run AI analysis on a media file using the latest models. Choose which parts to re-run via the flags below.

tools.name: bulk_move_media
tools.title: Bulk Move Media Files
tools.description: Move multiple media files to a folder in a single operation. Use this for batch reorganization instead of updating media one by one.

tools.name: upload_and_analyze_batch
tools.title: Upload and Analyze Several URLs
tools.description: Upload several URLs in one call — the batch form of upload_and_analyze, for when someone hands you a list of links. Takes up to 25 URLs and starts at most 5 at a time so a long list does not hammer the API. Each URL may be a direct/public file URL or a shareable social/video page link. Supported page links: YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, X/Twitter, Facebook, Reddit, SoundCloud, Twitch, Dailymotion, Streamable, Snapchat, Pinterest, Tumblr, Bilibili, VK, OK.ru and Rutube. Vimeo and Loom page links are not supported. One URL failing does not stop the rest: every URL is reported individually as uploaded or failed, with its reason. Returns as soon as the uploads are accepted, so poll get_media_status per mediaId, or list_media on the folder, to follow processing. Prefer this over calling upload_and_analyze in a loop.

categories.name: Ask AI Chat
categories.shortDescription: Run AI prompts across one file, a folder, or your whole workspace. Save favorites.

tools.name: ask_ai_chat
tools.title: Ask AI Chat
tools.description: Ask an AI-powered question about your media using Speak AI's AI Chat. Supports querying a single file, multiple files, entire folders, or your whole workspace. Pass mediaIds for specific files, folderIds for entire folders, or omit both to search across all media. Use assistantType to get specialized responses (e.g., 'researcher' for academic analysis, 'sales' for deal insights). To continue a conversation, pass the promptId from a previous response. Returns a promptId — save it to continue the conversation with follow-up questions. Set analysisMediaId + analysisInput to have the model listen to the audio or watch the video instead of reading the transcript alone. That is a premium feature and costs credits per hour of media — call get_analysis_quote first to check eligibility and price.

tools.name: retry_ai_chat
tools.title: Retry AI Chat
tools.description: Retry a failed or incomplete AI Chat response. Use when a previous ask_ai_chat call returned an error or incomplete answer.

tools.name: get_chat_history
tools.title: Get Chat History
tools.description: Get a list of recent AI Chat conversations. Returns conversation summaries with promptIds that can be used to continue conversations via ask_ai_chat or retrieve full messages via get_chat_messages.

tools.name: get_chat_messages
tools.title: Get Chat Messages
tools.description: Get full message history for conversations. Can filter by promptId for a specific conversation, by media/folder, or search across all chat messages. Returns questions, answers, references, and metadata.

tools.name: delete_chat_message
tools.title: Delete Chat Message
tools.description: Delete a specific chat message from conversation history.

tools.name: list_prompts
tools.title: List Prompt Templates
tools.description: List all available AI Chat templates. Use template IDs with ask_ai_chat's assistantTemplateId parameter when using assistantType 'custom'.

tools.name: get_favorite_prompts
tools.title: Get Favorite Prompts
tools.description: Get all prompts and answers that have been marked as favorites. Useful for finding saved insights and important AI-generated analysis.

tools.name: toggle_prompt_favorite
tools.title: Toggle Prompt Favorite
tools.description: Mark or unmark a chat message as a favorite for easy retrieval later.

tools.name: update_chat_title
tools.title: Rename Chat
tools.description: Update the title of a chat conversation for easier identification in history.

tools.name: submit_chat_feedback
tools.title: Submit Chat Feedback
tools.description: Submit feedback on a chat response (thumbs up/down). Helps improve AI answer quality.

tools.name: get_chat_statistics
tools.title: Get Chat Statistics
tools.description: Get usage statistics for AI Chat / chat. Returns metrics on prompt usage, optionally filtered by date range.

tools.name: export_chat_answer
tools.title: Export Chat Answer
tools.description: Export a specific AI Chat answer. Useful for saving AI-generated summaries, reports, or analysis results.

tools.name: get_analysis_quote
tools.title: Get Analysis Quote
tools.description: Check whether a media file can be analysed as audio or video, and what it will cost, before running ask_ai_chat with analysisInput. Returns { eligible, credits, seconds } and, when not eligible, a plain-English reason — an unavailable file is a normal result here, not an error. This is the only check that accounts for both the account's premium opt-in and the server-wide switch, so call it before committing to an expensive run.

categories.name: Search & analytics
categories.shortDescription: Full-text search across transcripts, insights, and metadata. Workspace-level stats.

tools.name: search_media
tools.title: Search Media Library
tools.description: Deep search across all media transcripts, insights, and metadata. Returns matching media with sentiment data, tags, and content excerpts. Use this to find specific topics, keywords, or themes across your entire library. For filtering by media type, folder, tags, or speakers, use the filterList parameter. Results are scoped by date range — defaults to current year if not specified.

tools.name: get_media_statistics
tools.title: Get Media Statistics
tools.description: Get workspace-level media statistics — total counts, processing status breakdown, storage usage, etc.

tools.name: list_supported_languages
tools.title: List Supported Languages
tools.description: List all languages supported for transcription. Use the language codes when uploading media with a specific sourceLanguage.

categories.name: Folders & views
categories.shortDescription: Create folders, save filtered views, bulk move files, share read-only collections.

tools.name: list_folders
tools.title: List Folders
tools.description: List all folders in the workspace with pagination and sorting.

tools.name: get_folder_info
tools.title: Get Folder Info
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific folder including its contents.

tools.name: create_folder
tools.title: Create Folder
tools.description: Create a new folder in the workspace.

tools.name: clone_folder
tools.title: Clone Folder
tools.description: Duplicate an existing folder and all of its contents.

tools.name: update_folder
tools.title: Update Folder
tools.description: Update a folder. `name` must always be supplied (the server replaces the folder config).

tools.name: delete_folder
tools.title: Delete Folder
tools.description: Permanently delete a folder. Media within the folder will be moved, not deleted.

tools.name: get_all_folder_views
tools.title: Get All Folder Views
tools.description: Retrieve all saved views across all folders.

tools.name: get_folder_views
tools.title: Get Folder Views
tools.description: Retrieve all saved views for a specific folder.

tools.name: create_folder_view
tools.title: Create Folder View
tools.description: Create a new saved view for a folder with a custom set of display columns.

tools.name: update_folder_view
tools.title: Update Folder View
tools.description: Update an existing saved view. Replaces the whole view, so `name`, `isDefault` and `columns` must all be supplied.

tools.name: clone_folder_view
tools.title: Clone Folder View
tools.description: Duplicate an existing folder view into a target folder.

categories.name: Recorders & surveys
categories.shortDescription: Public recording links for clients, prompted question sets, branded submission pages.

tools.name: create_recorder
tools.title: Create Recorder
tools.description: Create a new recorder or survey for collecting audio/video submissions.

tools.name: list_recorders
tools.title: List Recorders
tools.description: List all recorders/surveys in the workspace.

tools.name: get_recorder_info
tools.title: Get Recorder Info
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific recorder including its settings and questions.

tools.name: clone_recorder
tools.title: Clone Recorder
tools.description: Duplicate an existing recorder including all its settings and questions.

tools.name: get_recorder_recordings
tools.title: Get Recorder Submissions
tools.description: List all submissions/recordings collected by a specific recorder.

tools.name: generate_recorder_url
tools.title: Get Recorder Share URL
tools.description: Retrieve the existing shareable URL and embed iframe code for a recorder/survey. Read-only lookup: returns the recorder's pre-existing share link; it does not create, modify, or publish anything.

tools.name: update_recorder_settings
tools.title: Update Recorder Settings
tools.description: Update configuration settings for a recorder (branding, capture options, etc.). `name` must always be supplied.

tools.name: update_recorder_questions
tools.title: Update Recorder Questions
tools.description: Update the survey questions and respondent-info settings for a recorder.

tools.name: check_recorder_status
tools.title: Check Recorder Status
tools.description: Check whether a recorder/survey is active and accepting submissions.

tools.name: delete_recorder
tools.title: Delete Recorder
tools.description: Permanently delete a recorder/survey. Existing recordings are preserved.

categories.name: Clips
categories.shortDescription: Highlight clips from any time range. Export PDF, DOCX, SRT, VTT, TXT, CSV.

tools.name: create_clip
tools.title: Create Highlight Clip
tools.description: Create a highlight clip from one or more media files by specifying time ranges. Clips are processed asynchronously (states: queued, processing, completed, failed) — use get_clips to check status. Maximum total clip duration is 30 minutes. Use multiple timeRanges to stitch segments from different media files together.

tools.name: get_clips
tools.title: List Clips
tools.description: List clips, optionally filtered by folder or media files. If clipId is provided, returns a single clip with its download URL (when processed).

tools.name: update_clip
tools.title: Update Clip
tools.description: Update a clip's title, description, or tags.

tools.name: delete_clip
tools.title: Delete Clip
tools.description: Permanently delete a clip and its associated media file.

categories.name: Exports
categories.shortDescription: Highlight clips from any time range. Export PDF, DOCX, SRT, VTT, TXT, CSV.

tools.name: export_media
tools.title: Export Media Transcript
tools.description: Export a media file's transcript or insights in various formats (pdf, docx, srt, vtt, txt, csv).

tools.name: export_multiple_media
tools.title: Export Multiple Media Files
tools.description: Export multiple media files at once, optionally merged into a single file.

categories.name: Meeting bot
categories.shortDescription: Schedule Speak AI to join a Zoom / Google Meet / Teams call and transcribe automatically.

tools.name: list_meeting_events
tools.title: List Meeting Events
tools.description: List scheduled or completed meeting assistant events with filtering and pagination.

tools.name: schedule_meeting_event
tools.title: Schedule AI Meeting Assistant
tools.description: Schedule the Speak AI meeting assistant to join and record an upcoming meeting.

tools.name: remove_assistant_from_meeting
tools.title: Remove Assistant from Meeting
tools.description: Remove the Speak AI assistant from an active or scheduled meeting.

tools.name: delete_scheduled_assistant
tools.title: Cancel Scheduled Meeting Assistant
tools.description: Cancel and delete a scheduled meeting assistant event.

tools.name: get_live_meeting_transcript
tools.title: Get Live Meeting Transcript
tools.description: Fetch new sentences from an in-progress or just-ended meeting transcript. Identify the meeting via meetingAssistantEventId (preferred) or mediaId. Pass back the previous response's nextCursor as sinceEndInSec to receive only what's been added since.

categories.name: Automations
categories.shortDescription: Trigger actions on new recordings. Send events to your own backend.

tools.name: list_automations
tools.title: List Automations
tools.description: List automation rules in the workspace, with paging and filters.

tools.name: get_automation
tools.title: Get Automation Details
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific automation rule, including its trigger and step graph.

tools.name: create_automation
tools.title: Create Automation
tools.description: Create a new automation rule using the V2 graph model (trigger + ordered steps). Fetch valid step/trigger options with list_automation_triggers / list_automation_actions if unsure. For inbound-webhook automations the response includes inboundWebhook.inboundUrl (where to POST payloads) — recommended flow: create, send a test payload to the URL with ?test=1, call get_inbound_webhook to see mappable payload tokens, then update_automation to wire tokens/fieldsMap.

tools.name: update_automation
tools.title: Update Automation
tools.description: Update an existing automation rule. This replaces the whole automation (name, trigger, and steps), so fetch the current values with get_automation first and pass them all back with your changes.

tools.name: toggle_automation_status
tools.title: Toggle Automation Status
tools.description: Toggle an automation rule between active and inactive. This flips the current state — call get_automation first if you need to know which way it will flip.

tools.name: list_automation_names
tools.title: List Automation Names
tools.description: List automations as lightweight { name, id } pairs — useful for pickers without fetching full configs.

tools.name: get_automation_runs
tools.title: Get Automation Runs
tools.description: Get the run history (executions) for an automation, with paging and optional status filter.

tools.name: bulk_update_automation_status
tools.title: Bulk Update Automation Status
tools.description: Activate or deactivate multiple automations at once.

tools.name: bulk_assign_automation_folders
tools.title: Bulk Assign Automation Folders
tools.description: Set the folder scope for multiple automations at once. Pass an empty folderIds array to remove the folder restriction (run on all folders).

tools.name: run_automations
tools.title: Run Automations
tools.description: Manually run one or more automations against one or more media items now (outside the normal trigger).

tools.name: delete_automation
tools.title: Delete Automation
tools.description: Permanently delete an automation rule.

tools.name: list_automation_apps
tools.title: List Automation Apps
tools.description: List the apps available in the automation catalog (e.g. Speak native + connected integrations). Use to discover what triggers/actions exist before building an automation.

tools.name: list_automation_triggers
tools.title: List Automation Triggers
tools.description: List the trigger types available in the automation catalog. Optionally filter by app.

tools.name: list_automation_actions
tools.title: List Automation Actions
tools.description: List the action/step types available in the automation catalog. Optionally filter by app.

tools.name: build_automation
tools.title: Build Automation
tools.description: High-level automation builder: create (or update) a Speak automation from a friendly spec without knowing the wire format. Accepts folder/custom-field NAMES (resolved to ids; missing folders are auto-created), payload.<path> shorthand for webhook tokens, and simple step types (filter, branch, upload, ai_chat, translate, notify, call_webhook). For inbound-webhook automations the result includes the receive URL and mappable payload tokens. Prefer this over create_automation unless you need raw control.

categories.name: Webhooks
categories.shortDescription: Trigger actions on new recordings. Send events to your own backend.

tools.name: create_webhook
tools.title: Create Webhook
tools.description: Create a new webhook to receive real-time notifications when events occur in Speak AI.

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.title: List Webhooks
tools.description: List all configured webhooks in the workspace.

tools.name: update_webhook
tools.title: Update Webhook
tools.description: Update an existing webhook. This replaces the webhook config, so `callbackUrl` must always be supplied.

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.title: Delete Webhook
tools.description: Delete a webhook and stop receiving notifications at its endpoint.

tools.name: provision_inbound_webhook
tools.title: Provision Inbound Webhook
tools.description: Provision a standalone inbound webhook and get its public receive URL (inboundUrl) BEFORE creating an automation. Webhook-first flow: provision, send a test payload to the URL (append ?test=1 to only capture a sample without running anything), inspect mappable payload paths with get_inbound_webhook, then pass the webhookId as trigger.webhookId to create_automation.

tools.name: get_inbound_webhook
tools.title: Get Inbound Webhook
tools.description: Get an inbound webhook's public receive URL, captured sample payload, and the ready-to-paste {{trigger.payload.*}} tokens for mapping payload values into automation steps (speak-upload name/sourceUrl, fieldsMap custom-field values, notify/outbound-webhook templates). Pass either the webhookId or the automationId of an inbound-webhook automation. If no sample has been captured yet, send a test payload to the inboundUrl first (append ?test=1 to capture without running the automation).

tools.name: get_webhook_attempts
tools.title: Get Webhook Attempts
tools.description: Get the delivery log for an inbound webhook: each received request with its HTTP acknowledgement status (200 = sample captured, 202 = accepted and run started, 401/403 = rejected) and the automation run it started. Use get_automation_runs for the run outcomes themselves.

categories.name: Text notes
categories.shortDescription: Standalone AI-analyzed text notes plus custom fields you can tag any media file with.

tools.name: create_text_note
tools.title: Create Text Note
tools.description: Create a new text note in Speak AI for analysis. The content will be analyzed for insights, topics, and sentiment.

tools.name: get_text_insight
tools.title: Get Text Note Insights
tools.description: Retrieve AI-generated insights for a text note, including topics, sentiment, summaries, and action items.

tools.name: reanalyze_text
tools.title: Re-analyze Text Note
tools.description: Trigger a re-analysis of an existing text note to regenerate insights with the latest AI models.

tools.name: update_text_note
tools.title: Update Text Note
tools.description: Update an existing text note's name, content, or metadata. Updating text content will trigger re-analysis.

categories.name: Custom fields
categories.shortDescription: Standalone AI-analyzed text notes plus custom fields you can tag any media file with.

tools.name: list_fields
tools.title: List Custom Fields
tools.description: List all custom fields defined in the workspace. Each field returns a `slug` (for example `regulator_comment`) alongside its `id`, `name`, and `type`. Put `{{field.<slug>}}` in the prompt text you send and Speak substitutes that field's value for the media before the model sees it. A slug is unique per company and never changes when the field is renamed, so prefer it over the field name. A field with no slug yet resolves by `id` in the same token.

tools.name: create_field
tools.title: Create Custom Field
tools.description: Create a new custom field for categorizing and tagging media.

tools.name: update_field
tools.title: Update Custom Field
tools.description: Update a specific custom field by ID. `name` must always be supplied (the server replaces the field config).

tools.name: update_multiple_fields
tools.title: Bulk Update Custom Field Values
tools.description: Set custom field values across media in a single batch operation. Scope the update with `folderId` (all media in a folder) and/or `mediaIds`.

categories.name: Embed players
categories.shortDescription: Embeddable player widgets for media on your own website.

tools.name: create_embed
tools.title: Create Embed Widget
tools.description: Create an embeddable player/transcript widget for a media file or a set of folders. Provide `mediaId` for a single-media embed, or `folderIds` for a folder/library embed.

tools.name: update_embed
tools.title: Update Embed Widget
tools.description: Update an existing embed widget — appearance/feature toggles via `meta`, plus scope and privacy.

tools.name: check_embed
tools.title: Check Embed Exists
tools.description: Check if an embed exists for a media file and retrieve its configuration.

tools.name: get_embed_iframe_url
tools.title: Get Embed Iframe URL
tools.description: Get the iframe URL for embedding a media player/transcript on a webpage.

categories.name: Users & teams
categories.shortDescription: List workspace members and manage user groups.

tools.name: list_users
tools.title: List Users
tools.description: List the users (members) in the workspace/company, with their ids, names, emails, and permissions. Use the returned _id values when assigning members to user groups.

tools.name: list_user_groups
tools.title: List User Groups
tools.description: List all user groups in the company. Each group includes its members (hydrated names/emails) and member ids. Use this to discover group ids and current membership before updating or deleting a group.

tools.name: create_user_group
tools.title: Create User Group
tools.description: Create a new user group and assign members. Member ids come from list_users. Fails with a 409 if a group with the same name already exists in the company.

tools.name: update_user_group
tools.title: Update User Group
tools.description: Update a user group's name and member list. NOTE: the users array is a FULL REPLACEMENT, not a delta — any member id you omit is removed from the group. Fetch the current members with list_user_groups first and send the complete list.

tools.name: delete_user_group
tools.title: Delete User Group
tools.description: Delete a user group. This removes the group only; it does not delete the users themselves.

categories.name: Dashboards
categories.shortDescription: Create and manage analytics dashboards, widgets, and public sharing.

tools.name: list_dashboard_widgets
tools.title: List Dashboard Widgets
tools.description: Discovery + how-to helper for building and customizing dashboards. Returns every widget type with what it shows and the exact strict `config` shape it accepts, the shared vocabulary (metric grammar, groupBy, per-widget binding, filters, thresholds, sources, date-range presets, sections), design rules for composing a dashboard that reads well, two complete worked example payloads, and tips for managing dashboards. Call this before create_dashboard / update_dashboard.

tools.name: list_dashboards
tools.title: List Dashboards
tools.description: List all analytics dashboards the caller can access, including share state and each dashboard's current `revision` (needed for update_dashboard).

tools.name: get_dashboard
tools.title: Get Dashboard
tools.description: Get a single dashboard's full spec: title, description, source, date range, sections, widgets, and the current `revision` (pass that revision back to update_dashboard).

tools.name: create_dashboard
tools.title: Create Dashboard
tools.description: Create an analytics dashboard. Only `title` is required — source defaults to the whole workspace and dateRange to last30days. Add widgets by listing their types (the MCP assigns ids and lays them out automatically), scope with source ({type:"folders",folderIds} | {type:"team"} | {type:"workspace"}) and dateRange ({preset}), and optionally group widgets into sections. Design guidance: lead with a narrative widget as the first widget; group sections by the QUESTION they answer, not by widget type; don't pad — every widget earns its place (aim for 4-16 widgets on a full build); if something can't be expressed by the widget catalog, put it in a narrative widget's focus instead of faking it. Call list_dashboard_widgets first for the widget catalog, config vocabulary, design rules, and full examples.

tools.name: update_dashboard
tools.title: Update Dashboard
tools.description: Update a dashboard. Two modes. (1) Metadata-only: pass just icon/assignTo/filters/isDefault — no spec fields, no revision needed. (2) Spec update: pass the FULL spec — title, source, dateRange, sections, widgets — plus `revision`. Widgets and sections are REPLACED, not merged, so call get_dashboard first and resend everything you want to keep. `revision` is the optimistic-concurrency token from get_dashboard/list_dashboards: the server accepts the write only if it still matches, then increments it. A 409 conflict means another writer saved first — re-fetch with get_dashboard, rebuild your changes on the fresh spec, and retry with the new revision.

tools.name: delete_dashboard
tools.title: Delete Dashboard
tools.description: Soft-delete a dashboard. This also deactivates its public share link.

tools.name: duplicate_dashboard
tools.title: Duplicate Dashboard
tools.description: Clone an existing dashboard. The copy gets fresh widget ids, a "<name> (copy)" title, cleared sharing, and its revision reset to 0. Ideal for cloning a fully-configured dashboard, then tweaking it via update_dashboard.

tools.name: share_dashboard
tools.title: Share Dashboard
tools.description: Enable public sharing for a dashboard and return its share token + embed id. WARNING: by default the public link resolves with no passphrase, so anyone with the token can view the dashboard data until an owner sets one.

tools.name: get_dashboard_speakers_insight
tools.title: Get Dashboard Speakers Insight
tools.description: Compute a speakers breakdown for a given folder scope, date range, and field filters. Standalone analytics — does not require a dashboard to exist.
